items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 7:1
items.html: Malchut, when it is revealed, is hinted at by the name ani ('I'), and when it is concealed it is hinted at by the name hu ('He'). And in the Malchut of the corners of the head it is called hu, because there is no revealed aspect of the female there. And this is because the hairs of the head are corrected in the aspect of the MEM of Tzelem (see Answer 10), and therefore no power of the female and of restriction can be revealed there. (Part 1, Page 384, Item 183).
